title: Effects of Bone Augmentation on Implant Success and Survival: A Retrospective Analysis With 6-Year Mean Follow-Up
authors: Tatli, U., Cavana, A., Tukel, H. C., & Benlidayi, M. E. (2025). Clinical implant dentistry and related research, 27(2), e70021.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss Jason membrane (porcine pericardium) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “The implants placed in augmented bone showed similar cumulative success and survival rates compared to implants placed in natural bone with a 6-year mean follow-up. The augmentation group showed lower esthetic scores. There are some differences in clinical parameters among augmentation groups; however, all the augmentation groups showed similar success and survival rates” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
